answer: Bonded escrows make identities costly to duplicate: when k coordinated validators equivocate, linked evidence triggers a correlated slash proportional to k(k−1), hence O(k²), rather than isolated per-key penalties. Detection then applies asymmetric depreciation to seized collateral, making swarm-wide capital loss grow with an exponential-in-k multiplier. Mirror-linked logs expose common control; nectar-like rewards cannot offset the risk, and a willow-thin identity split offers no protection.
